defects.name: clip_action is silent, binds on real actions, and differs between the two agents
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:197-206 (do_clip guard :197, jnp.clip :205); conf/agent/signatures.yaml:16 (clip_action: 10.0) versus conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:14 (clip_action: null)
defects.claim: The array passes no clip_action, so the actor-critic projects the control componentwise onto [-10, 10] while the value gradient applies none; because every shipped R is diagonal (measured R = 0.1*I on platoon_h1h2 and the Hopfield cells) the projected control is the exact greedy control of a box-constrained problem whose constraint appears nowhere in the declared objective J, and whose value functional is not the V the critic fits. Instrumented ContinuousValueGradient runs on platoon_h1h2 (kind=signature, depth=2, 25 episodes, identical seed) measure 455 of 7525 actions clipped (6.0%) at clip_action=10.0 versus 0 of 7525 at null, with peak |u|_inf pinned at exactly 10 against 32.69 and the closed-loop trajectory altered (peak ||x|| 10.68 against 26.84). The clip is never logged; note the 6.0% figure is measured in an AC-vs-VG-code probe on platoon_h1h2, not on the five campaign cells.

defects.name: Target-network lag contaminates dV/dt in the continuous-time temporal-difference residual
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:259-265 (critic_loss); conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:18 (tau_polyak: 0.01)
defects.claim: V_t is evaluated with critic_params and V_next with Polyak-averaged target_params, so (V_next - V_t)/dt equals dV_online/dt + (V_target - V_online)(s')/dt: the second term is absent from Doya's semi-gradient, which prescribes a stop-gradient on the same function, not a second lagged function, and it is amplified by 1/dt. Measured over 3000 transitions (hopfield_nonlinear, value_gradient, seed 42, dt = 0.1, tau_polyak = 0.01), the mean spurious lag term is 2.850e-01 against a mean |dV/dt| of 1.193e-01 computed with the single online network — 2.39 times larger than the derivative it perturbs, and 32.3% of the magnitude of the residual. The config flag algorithm.semi_gradient is never read in this agent, so the stop-gradient is unconditional.

defects.name: ContinuousValueGradient window spans tau + 3*dt, not [-tau, 0]
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:59-61 (_compute_window_size), consumed at :56-57 and :86 (window_length = window_size + 1)
defects.claim: _compute_window_size returns int(np.ceil(max_delay / self.env.step_size)) + 3, so the critic's domain strictly contains the delay differential equation's state x_t on [-tau, 0]; the '+3' has no justification in code, comment, or git history (git log -S "+ 3 if max_delay" returns only the import commit a02cc92). Measured spans with x64 enabled: linear_dde_scalar 1.60 against tau = 1.0, MG_1D_chaotic 17.75 against 17.0, hopfield_linear/nonlinear 0.80 against 0.5, platoon_h1h2 0.35 against 0.2. The excess taps are not inert: per-tap sensitivity on linear_dde_scalar gives ||dV/d(taps older than -tau)||/||dV/d(taps in [-tau,0])|| = 0.3074 at initialisation and 0.1921 after 20 episodes, so the greedy control is not a state feedback for the plant.

defects.name: CTACSignatureJAX window spans tau + dt, and disagrees with the value gradient's window at fixed cell
defects.location: src/agents/signatures_jax.py:162-165
defects.claim: The actor-critic's window computation adds +1 tap where the value gradient adds +3, so at fixed representation and fixed cell the two agents observe different-length paths (measured on linear_dde_scalar: 8 taps against 6; platoon_h1h2 with x64: 8 against 6) even though the campaign forces force_signature_window=true with an explicit per-cell WIN. Both constants are undocumented and both over-span the mathematical window [-tau, 0]. Any residual difference in the resolved window between the two agents is a direct agent-asymmetry confound for the 150-task campaign and must be resolved against the forced WIN values before launch.

defects.name: The taps outside [-tau, 0] are fabricated at reset by constant front-padding of phi
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:146-173 (_fill_buffer_initial, pad branch :167-171); mirrored at src/agents/signatures_jax.py:270-280
defects.claim: wrapper.initial_conditions returns exactly the environment buffer, which spans exactly tau; since the agent window needs 3 (value gradient) or 1 (signatures) further taps, the else branch front-pads with subsampled[0], inventing a constant extension of phi to the left of phi's own support on every reset (measured pad counts: 3/1 on linear_dde_scalar, hopfield_linear, MG_1D_limit_cycle, platoon_h1h2). The fabrication is currently masked numerically only because fix_initial_state makes phi constant; with a non-constant history_function the window would open on a spurious flat segment, and the excess-tap sensitivity is non-zero regardless.

defects.name: divergence_threshold truncates the episode and its reported cost, without logging
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:616-630 (_is_episode_done :628); src/agents/signatures_jax.py:456; src/agents/CSAC_jax.py:634; conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:16, conf/agent/signatures.yaml:25 (100.0), src/configs.py:39 (default 50.0)
defects.claim: When ||x|| exceeds the threshold the episode ends and the objective integral is truncated, so the reported cost of a truncated episode is not the cost of a completed one; the truncation is silent and biases the metric in the direction that hides divergence. Measured not to fire on the runs exercised (no current number contaminated), but within a factor 3.7 of binding on platoon_h1h2. The campaign passes 100.0 explicitly to both agents, closing the value-asymmetry, so the residue is the silence and the truncation bias itself, not a differing threshold.

defects.name: lstd_reg is an absolute ridge in one branch and a trace-relative ridge in the other, on a numerically singular system
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:727/729 (rank > 0 branch, self._lstd_reg * abs(trace(Mk)/rank)) against :734/736 (rank = 0 branch, absolute self._lstd_reg * eye(d)); :739 (silent non-finite skip); conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:76 (lstd_reg: 1.0e-3)
defects.claim: The same nominal lstd_reg carries different units in the two branches, and M is accumulated as an unnormalised sum with exponential forgetting, so the absolute ridge's effective strength drifts with the number of transitions. Measured on the scalar linear delay differential equation after 12 episodes (d = 12): ||M||_2 = 3.876e8, sigma_min = 9.05e-14, cond = 4.283e21, so the shipped 1e-3 has relative strength 2.58e-12 and acts only on the null subspace; on hopfield_nonlinear (d = 30, 40 episodes) cond(M) reaches 1e24-1e31 and reg/sigma_min exceeds 5e9, so the ridge selects the solution outright rather than perturbing a fixed point, and ||theta|| is measured non-monotonic in reg (2.776e6, 2.788e6, 2.902e6, 4.820e6, 1.337e6, 1.103e5 across 1e-8 to 1.0). The ridge is unlogged.

defects.name: The origin_augmentation basepoint is read from a tap outside the state, and breaks Chen's identity on a sliding window
defects.location: src/utils/dynamic_signature.py:199-203 (origin = data[0] * elapsed_fraction), docstring :170-196; fed by the over-long window from src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:59-61
defects.claim: The ramp channel injects data[0], the oldest tap, which lies at t - tau - 3*dt (value gradient) or t - tau - dt (signatures) rather than at t - tau, and at reset that point is a fabricated pad value; the basepoint is also re-based on every sliding window, which is not the Arribas basepoint construction. Measured per-tap sensitivity on linear_dde_scalar concentrates entirely on tap 0 and the endpoint ([0.005, 0, ..., 0.016] at initialisation; [0.002, 0, ..., 0.011] after 20 episodes), making tap 0 — a point outside [-tau, 0] — the largest non-endpoint contributor to V, and hence the mechanism by which the over-long window binds.

defects.name: force_signature_window inverts its documented polarity and the configured window_size is dead
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:56-57; src/agents/signatures_jax.py:164-167; conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:47 (window_size: 40), :53 ("force_signature_window: false  # if true, override window_size to match max delay")
defects.claim: The comment states the flag forces the delay-derived window when true, whereas the code derives the window when the flag is FALSE and honours the configured window_size only when true; with the shipped default the yaml's window_size: 40 is silently discarded (measured used windows 8 / 6 on linear_dde_scalar). The campaign sets force_signature_window=true with an explicit per-cell WIN, so the flag reads the intended way there; the residue is that every pre-campaign artefact and every default-path invocation carries the inverted meaning.

defects.name: np.linalg.lstsq(..., rcond=None) is a silent truncated-SVD estimator on the H1/H2 fit
defects.location: run/study/h1h2_evaluation.py:378; run/study/mwe_e0_nn_critic.py:158; run/study/diagnose_optimization_floor.py:88; run/study/mwe_real_platoon_offmanifold_cheat.py:171
defects.claim: rcond=None selects numpy's default cutoff max(M,N)*eps, so the solve discards every singular direction below roughly 4e-13 relative: the estimator is rank-truncated and regularised, not plain least squares, and the truncation is data-dependent — it fires on the signature arm, whose design matrix is near-rank-deficient by construction (shuffle identities), and not on the Markovian arm. Measured spectra (seed 0, on_off_sheet, n_off=500): cell markovian — signature rank 22/30 with 8 directions discarded (cond 4.476e17) while markovian is 5/5 and raw_history 65/65; cell linear_dde — signature 8/12 with 4 discarded (cond 1.913e17). The representation comparison is therefore between a truncated estimator and untruncated ones.

defects.name: noise.smooth builds a Gaussian-process exploration path whose kernel is numerically the identity
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:410-447 (kernel :425, Cholesky jitter :428, sample :443-446); src/agents/signatures_jax.py:662; conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:40 (length_scale: 0.002) and conf/agent/signatures.yaml (0.02), against src/configs.py:66 (default 0.2)
defects.claim: At the shipped length scales the squared-exponential kernel evaluated on the control grid is the identity to machine precision, so the delivered exploration is white noise rather than the smooth path the flag names — and the two agents ship length scales differing by a factor of ten, an additional asymmetry. The purpose of smooth exploration on a delay plant is to excite the history window coherently, which does not occur; the exploration signal is not the measured quantity, so no reported cost is directly corrupted.

defects.name: The delay differential equation's initial condition is sampled as a point, never as a path
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:137-140 (_sample_initial_state), :500 and :675 (wrapper.reset called without history_function); src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:71-77 (constant-tile fallback, data_history = jnp.tile(self.x0, (buffer_size, 1)))
defects.claim: The initial condition of the plant is a path phi in C([-tau, 0], R^d), yet _sample_initial_state draws a point from a normal distribution and the wrapper tiles it into a constant history; history_function is unreachable from every call site. The sampler's support is therefore the constant paths, a measure-zero subset of the path space — the same class of error as the retired actor-critic preheat, on the same object. Dormant as a sampler on the shipped config only because fix_initial_state collapses the distribution to a single constant path, which means the delay testbed has never been exercised from a non-constant initial path.

defects.name: _evaluate_noiseless ignores the divergence and non-finite guards: training and evaluation use different termination rules
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:684 (while not self._is_episode_done(x_t, time_only=True)) against :520 (self._is_episode_done(x_t)); guards at :626-629
defects.claim: Training episodes terminate on ||x|| > divergence_threshold or on a non-finite state, whereas the noiseless evaluation rollout runs to the time horizon regardless. The reported evaluation cost and the training cost are therefore integrals over differently-defined episodes, and a divergent evaluation rollout is integrated to completion rather than cut.

defects.name: The LSTD accumulator applies the discount unconditionally, ignoring discount.discounted
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:308 (diff = (phi_n - phi_t)/dt - phi_c/tau) against the semi-gradient path at :262-264; conf/agent/value_gradient.yaml:29-30 (discounted: false, tau: 100.0)
defects.claim: critic_loss subtracts V_t/tau only under `if discounted:`, whereas the LSTD path forms the discounted difference with no reference to self.discount.discounted, so algorithm.lstd: true silently switches the estimator to a discounted fixed point the configuration explicitly disclaims. Measured on 183 transitions from 10 episodes on the scalar linear delay differential equation (d = 12): at the shipped tau = 100.0, ||theta_code|| = 1.696e6 against ||theta_undiscounted|| = 1.722e6, a 1.47% relative difference with cosine 0.999999; the divergence grows at the signatures.yaml value tau = 1.0.

defects.name: runge_kutta4 is second-order on the delay differential equation, not fourth
defects.location: src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:53-59 (runge_kutta4), :45-51 (dynamics); src/utils/solver_buffer_jax.py:36-62 (get_delayed_interpolated, linear interpolation at :62)
defects.claim: The stage evaluations obtain the delayed state by linear interpolation between bracketing buffer samples, whose local error is O(h^2); by the standard min(p, q+1) result for Runge-Kutta schemes on delay differential equations this caps the global order at 2 regardless of the fourth-order tableau. Measured by a convergence study on xdot = -x - 2x(t-1) with constant history against a method-of-steps reference at rtol 1e-13: absolute errors 2.874e-03 down to 2.807e-06 over six halvings of h, giving an observed order of exactly 2.000 at every refinement. The discretisation is legitimate in kind, but the claimed order is wrong and the step sizes chosen on a fourth-order assumption do not deliver the assumed accuracy.

defects.name: The signature feature Gram is numerically singular: effective rank about 5 of 30
defects.location: src/representations/signature.py:48-51; consumed by src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:108 (linear critic readout)
defects.claim: Measured on 400 sampled windows (n_state = 2, window_length = 41, depth = 2, origin_augmentation = true): cond(G) = 9.400e20 and effective rank (spectral entropy) 4.95 out of a feature dimension of 30, so roughly 25 of 30 directions lie at or below the double-precision noise floor. The linear readout is identified in only about five directions and the remainder is fixed by the solver's tie-breaking rather than by the data — density at infinite depth is not realisability at finite depth on finite data. Present on every run that fits the linear critic; the downstream effect on the reported cost is not measured.

defects.name: The initial path phi is narrowed to float32 inside an otherwise float64 window pipeline
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:163, :166, :171 (np.asarray(x/self.training.scale, dtype=np.float32)); src/agents/CSAC_jax.py:326; against src/representations/factory.py:65/73/89 (buffers declared float64)
defects.claim: _fill_buffer_initial narrows the delay differential equation's initial condition — the very object the recent phi-loading work was undertaken to represent correctly — to single precision, leaving the window mixed-precision; measured relative perturbation 3e-8, propagating to the control at the 1e-7 level. The project owner has decided this cast STAYS: removing it would invalidate the existing 5-seed H1/H2 value-gradient results, which must remain bit-reproducible. Registered as a known, deliberate residue rather than an actionable fix.

defects.name: The resolved window is never persisted: every run's config.yaml records a window that was not used
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:56-57 and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:164-165 (mutate the dataclass, not cfg); main_unified.py:331 ((run_dir / "config.yaml").write_text(OmegaConf.to_yaml(cfg)))
defects.claim: build_agent constructs a fresh SignatureConfig dataclass from cfg (train.py:111) and the agents mutate that dataclass; the Hydra cfg is untouched and is written to config.yaml before train() runs, so the persisted provenance records the nominal window, never the derived one. Measured on linear_dde_scalar: value_gradient used window_size = 8 and signatures 6 while config.yaml persists 40; all 450 persisted run configs under data/ carry force_signature_window: false, so every recorded window_size (2, 5, 6, 10, 20, 23, 28, 43, 70) was silently overridden and none is the window used.

defects.name: training.scale is absent from the control-law chain rule: the implemented control is scale times the greedy control
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:199-206 (end_gradient = grad_path[-1]; u = 1/2 * inv(R) @ B.T @ end_gradient), with the scaling introduced at :163, :166, :171, :336, :346, :450, :691; src/agents/signatures_jax.py:93
defects.claim: The buffer holds x/scale and the gradient is taken with respect to the SCALED endpoint, but the result is applied as if it were grad_{x(t)}V, omitting the factor 1/scale; the executed control is therefore exactly scale times the Doya law while the reward is computed from the physical state. Latent, not armed, in this campaign: every agent config sets training.scale = 1.0 and conf/agent/signatures.yaml:72 sets network.normalize_entries = false, so signatures_jax.py:93 (which would set scale = divergence_threshold = 100.0) does not fire — verified. It remains a foot-gun that a future config arming normalize_entries would trigger silently.

defects.name: _evaluate_noiseless consumes the training RNG stream, so the evaluation cadence changes the training trajectory
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:674 (jax.random.split(self.key) inside the evaluation rollout), invoked at :580-581 under `if episode % self.training.eval_interval == 0`
defects.claim: The evaluation splits self.key — the same key the exploration noise draws from at :245 and :442 — and never restores it, so the number of splits consumed before any training step depends on eval_interval and two runs with the same master seed diverge as soon as their cadences differ. Measured on the scalar linear delay differential equation (seed 42, 6 episodes, otherwise identical): eval_interval = 2 gives episodic costs [-1.7897, -1.4170, -1.6219, -1.3523, -1.1869, -1.4540] against [-1.7897, -1.4170, -1.6219, -1.3289, -1.1893, -1.4627] at eval_interval = 3 — identical until the first cadence divergence, then different. This violates the shared-seed policy and becomes an agent-asymmetry confound if the two agents' eval_interval defaults differ.

defects.name: The temporal-difference difference quotient is first-order and the running reward is sampled at the step's right endpoint, with neither convention stated
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:259-265 (td_error = reward + (V_next - V_t)/dt), :693 (total_cost += float(reward) * step_size); src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:88 (reward computed from final_state)
defects.claim: dV/dt is a first-order forward difference paired with a right-endpoint reward and a left-endpoint discount; the scheme is consistent and first-order accurate, so no reported number is demonstrably wrong, but the order is never stated and consistency is never checked on cells whose own config comments identify dt as the dominant conditioning lever. Registered as a discretisation whose arithmetic must be documented, not as an error.

defects.name: Subsampling strides from the oldest sample, so the window endpoint is not guaranteed to be x(t)
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:157-158 (subsampled = history_data[::self.env.resolution]) and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:276; source array src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:176-193 (JAXEnvWrapper.initial_conditions), buffer capacity at :31
defects.claim: initial_conditions returns the solver-cadence history oldest-first with ordered_data[-1] = x(t0); striding forward from index 0 retains the endpoint if and only if (capacity - 1) % resolution == 0, an arithmetic coincidence that no line asserts. Measured across all 22 environment configs the remainder is 0 for every delayed cell (MG_1D_chaotic 341/5, hopfield_linear/nonlinear, linear_dde_scalar, platoon_h1h2, etc.), so it does not fire on any shipped configuration; if it did, the vertical (Dupire) derivative at the endpoint — the object the control law needs — would silently be taken at the wrong point.

defects.name: float32 narrowing of tau turns ceil(tau/dt) into an off-by-one, adding a phantom tap
defects.location: src/envs/env_rk_jax.py:20 (self.delay = jnp.array(delay)), consumed by value_gradient_jax.py:60 and signatures_jax.py:162
defects.claim: Without jax_enable_x64 the config's float64 delay narrows to 0.20000000298023224 on platoon_h1h2, so tau/dt = 4.0000000596 and np.ceil returns 5 rather than 4 — one phantom tap from a representation artefact, giving 9/7 taps instead of 8/6. Measured to be scoped out of the canonical path: main_unified.py:63 sets jax_enable_x64=True and test/conftest.py:9 does likewise, so the campaign is unaffected and the test suite cannot catch it; it fires under any bare import of src.agents or an ad-hoc script that omits the flag.

defects.name: Hard-coded fallback window of 10 taps when tau = 0
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:61 (`... else 10`) and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:163 (`... else 10`)
defects.claim: For a memoryless plant the window collapses to the point x(t), yet both agents impose a magic 10-tap window, i.e. 1.0 s of history at dt = 0.1, with no justification in code or comment. The campaign's markovian cell (double_integrator) passes WIN=10 explicitly with force_signature_window=true, so the forced value coincides with the fallback and the two agents agree there; the constant remains undocumented and is the default on any non-forced invocation.

defects.name: A study named for the window sweep neither sets nor uses the window it labels
defects.location: run/MG_transient/run_comparison_window_size.py:55-56, 71-72, 87-88, 104-105, 121-122
defects.claim: The script interpolates ${agent.signature.window_size} into wandb.name and eval_data_name for all five arms but never assigns window_size and never sets force_signature_window, so with the default (false) every arm uses the delay-derived window and the labels report the untouched yaml value. Measured at the mechanism level: the used window (8 / 6 on linear_dde_scalar) differs from the interpolated value (40), so the labels are wrong by construction; whether any figure from this script has been cited is not measured.

defects.name: abs(I) > 1e8 cost cap and non-finite-control abort substitute a sentinel for the H1/H2 rollout cost
defects.location: run/study/h1h2_evaluation.py:355-356 (`if not np.all(np.isfinite(u)) or abs(I) > 1e8: return np.array(Ws), float("inf")`), consumed at :428 (margin)
defects.claim: Both guards abandon the rollout mid-horizon and return +infinity, which is a sentinel rather than the truncated integral; the margin (I_base - I_test)/(|I_base| + 1e-18) then evaluates to inf, -inf or nan and the HOLDS/fails verdict is decided by a comparison against infinity, while summary.json stores I = Infinity with no record of which guard fired. Not measured firing: on hopfield_linear (seed 0, on_off_sheet, n_off = 200) the reported costs were I_nc = 128.55, I* = 0.0959, I_cl in [0.097, 0.116] — five to nine orders below the cap, with no non-finite control over 2567 steps; behaviour on platoon, mg_limit_cycle and mg_chaotic is not measured.

defects.name: float32 narrowing of the deployment window in the H1/H2 harness creates a train/deploy dtype mismatch
defects.location: run/study/h1h2_evaluation.py:350, :359; same pattern in run/study/mwe_truncation_ridge_sweep.py:100/107/155/205, mwe_platoon_neighbourhood_sweep.py:71/80/125, mwe_real_platoon_offmanifold_cheat.py:78/84/119
defects.claim: The rollout window is narrowed to float32 at every append while the training windows on which theta is fitted are float64 (measured dtype float64, shape (1700, 6, 1) on linear_dde), so the estimator is fitted on one window space and deployed on another. Measured effect on the cell exercised (linear_dde, seed 0, n_off = 500): re-rolling the identical theta in float64 shifts I_cl by 1.466e-08 (markovian), 1.121e-08 (raw_history), 3.319e-09 (signature) relative — the narrowing fires but is inert at the reported precision on this cell.

defects.name: state_augmentation is exactly linearly redundant and aborts the run if enabled
defects.location: src/agents/signatures_jax.py:197-202 (init), :503-504 (train path), :734-736 (get_eval_action); declared only in conf/agent/signatures.yaml
defects.claim: With origin_augmentation = true the depth-1 terms give x_i(t) = S^{X_i} + S^{ramp_i} identically, so the state channels add no information — verified numerically, regressing x(t) on the signature features gives a relative residual of 9.0e-16 with origin_augmentation on, against 1.5e-1 with it off. Measured unreachable: every config sets state_augmentation: false, and enabling it aborts at the first evaluation callback rather than corrupting a number silently, which is the benign failure mode.

defects.name: signature.time_origin, signature.state_augmentation and algorithm.semi_gradient are dead parameters in the value-gradient path
defects.location: src/configs.py:82-86, :107, :150, :210; src/representations/factory.py:28-53 and src/representations/signature.py:22-42 (neither forwarded); consumers at src/utils/dynamic_signature.py:122, :130, :164, :206
defects.claim: SignatureConfig declares state_augmentation and time_origin, but make_representation accepts neither and SlidingSignatureJAX is constructed without them, so the value-gradient agent's behaviour is independent of both keys; the window clock is consequently dimensionless (jnp.linspace(0.0, time_origin, n) always receives the default). algorithm.semi_gradient is likewise never read by value_gradient_jax.py. Measured inert because every shipped setting equals the default; a config key that silently does nothing is nonetheless a reproducibility hazard.

defects.name: The adaptive noise schedule's clip and epsilon are inert at the shipped configuration but uncommented
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:223 (noise_scale = jnp.clip((V_TARGET - V_t)/(V_TARGET - V_BAD + 1e-6), 0.1, 1.0)); identical construct at src/agents/signatures_jax.py:387; defaults at src/configs.py:63, :198
defects.claim: The schedule clips the noise scale to [0.1, 1.0] and floors a denominator with 1e-6; measured dead in the shipped configs (the adaptive branch is not selected) but live in the dataclass defaults, so an invocation that omits the yaml key arms it. No comment states the inertness, which the project's clamp rule requires.

defects.name: The dt <= 1e-9 guard substitutes a fabricated step size rather than failing
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:348-349 (`if dt <= 1e-9: dt = 1e-4  # Avoid division by zero`); identical at src/agents/base_jax.py:243-244 and src/agents/signatures_jax.py:489
defects.claim: Presented as a division guard, the line silently replaces the temporal-difference step by an unrelated magic constant 1e-4, which would corrupt the residual rather than raise. Provably inert on every shipped config — no step size comes within seven orders of magnitude of 1e-9 — but the code carries no comment stating why it is inert, which the project's clamp rule requires for an unlogged guard.

defects.name: Cholesky jitter K += 1e-6 * I on the exploration-noise covariance
defects.location: src/agents/value_gradient_jax.py:428 (K += 1e-6 * np.eye(n_points))
defects.claim: A fixed absolute jitter is added to the exploration kernel before factorisation, unlogged and unjustified relative to the kernel's scale. D ("necessary discretisation; the arithmetic must be right") is the correct bin: a discrete window covering the continuous interval [-tau,0] is a genuine and necessary discretisation, and ceil(tau/dt) is the right arithmetic. The "+3" is an unjustified margin ON TOP of correct arithmetic — no RK stage needs history older than -tau (intermediate stages at t+c*dt require delayed values at t+c*dt-tau, which are NEWER than t-tau), and for both affected cells tau is an exact multiple of dt (1.0/0.2 = 5, 17.0/0.25 = 68), so no straddling interpolation margin is needed either. `git log -S "+ 3 if max_delay"` returning only the import commit a02cc92 is consistent with the margin being unexamined rather than reasoned.

result.agent_asymmetric: YES — and this is the decisive finding, larger than the defect as framed. The asymmetry is structural, not parametric: `grep -c "target_params" src/agents/signatures_jax.py` returns **0**. The signatures agent has no target network whatsoever. Quoting both critic losses at HEAD (5b410d6): value_gradient_jax.py:261-262 reads `V_t = critic.apply(critic_params, sig_t).squeeze()` / `V_next = critic.apply(jax.lax.stop_gradient(target_params), sig_next).squeeze()`, whereas signatures_jax.py:618-619 reads `V_t = critic.apply(critic_params, sig_t).squeeze()` / `V_next = critic.apply(jax.lax.stop_gradient(critic_params), sig_next).squeeze()`. The signatures agent therefore implements Doya's semi-gradient exactly — stop-gradient on the *same* function — so its lag term is identically zero by construction (no measurement required; the two applications share one params object). The value-gradient agent bootstraps from a *second, lagged* function. At fixed representation the two agents regress different critic targets. The asymmetry is compounded at initialisation: value_gradient_jax.py:108-110 splits `key_critic, key_target, self.key = jax.random.split(self.key, 3)` and initialises the target from an **independent** key, so the target does not start as a copy of the critic — the probe measured `max|critic_params - target_params| at init = 3.397e-02`, against `network.std_init: 0.01`. The defect is agent-asymmetric across all three representations and all five cells, since none of the three REPARG variants touches the critic bootstrap. It is not asymmetric *between* representations.

Any fix (dropping the target network to match signatures_jax.py:619, or initialising `target_params` from `key_critic` so the target starts as a copy) alters `critic_loss`, hence the critic gradient, hence `critic_params` at every step, hence the control law `u = -(1/2) R^{-1} g^T grad_x V` which reads `self.critic_params` (value_gradient_jax.py:241). The consequence for the launch decision must be stated plainly rather than resolved here. The auditor's implicit remedy (apply the guard in eval) is not obviously an improvement, and is worth stating because the intuition runs the wrong way: cutting a divergent rollout early yields a SHORTER, hence LESS NEGATIVE, integral, which scores BETTER under the `eval > best` argmax. Guarding therefore partially REWARDS divergence. It happens not to flip the argmax here only because the cut values (-21238.63, -13619.99) remain far worse than the non-divergent -296.45. A correct remedy scores a truncated rollout as strictly worse than any completed one — e.g. return -inf on a cut, or charge the remaining horizon at the divergent cost — rather than merely applying the training guard verbatim.

Both augmentation channels are affine in the normalised window time s: dynamic_signature.py builds the origin channel as `origin = data[0] * elapsed_fraction` with `elapsed_fraction = jnp.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n)` and the time channel as `time_channel = jnp.linspace(0.0, time_origin, n)` with time_origin = 1.0. Writing the augmented channels (t, X, a s) with a = X_0, the depth-2 signature satisfies for EVERY window: S^1 = 1 (constant), S^{11} = 1/2 = (1/2) S^1, S^{1,o_i} = S^{o_i,1} = (1/2) S^{o_i}, S^{o_i,o_j} = S^{o_j,o_i}, and the shuffle relation against the constant channel S^{1,j} + S^{j,1} = S^1 S^j = S^j. Counting the independent linear relations gives co-rank 4 for n_state = 1 (feature dimension 12, predicted rank 8) and co-rank 8 for n_state = 2 (feature dimension 30, predicted rank 22). The measured numerical ranks are 8 of 12 on linear_dde and mg_chaotic and 22 of 30 on both Hopfield cells — an exact match to the prediction; double_integrator measures 20 of 30, i.e. two further trajectory-specific dependencies on top of the structural eight. So 27-33 % of the readout's coordinates are provably unidentifiable by construction, independently of the data, and the gap between numerical rank and effective rank (1.08-3.91) is the data-driven near-degeneracy on top.

NOT MEASURED. The downstream effect on the reported cost is not measured, as the auditor conceded. Whether the zero-gradient coordinates leak into the control law through the vertical derivative d phi / d x(t) — the ker G gradient gap — is not measured here.
